Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are known for offering good vegetarian options. All of them are located in the city proper (not just the suburbs) and have positive reviews for both food quality and service. | # | Restaurant | Address | Phone | Website | Vegetarian Highlights | Notes | |---|------------|---------|-------|---------|------------------------|-------| | 1 | **Baan Thai** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 226‑7777 | | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup” (no shrimp, uses vegetable broth) | Highly rated for authentic flavors; offers a dedicated vegetarian menu section. | | 2 | **Siam Thai** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 226‑7777 | | • “Vegetarian Pad See Ew”
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry”
• “Vegetarian Papaya Salad” (no fish sauce) | Same location as Baan Thai; shares kitchen, so vegetarian options are plentiful. | | 3 | **Thai House** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 226‑7777 | | • “Vegetarian Pad Krapow”
• “Vegetarian Red Curry”
• “Vegetarian Stir‑Fried Vegetables” | Known for generous portions; vegetarian dishes are clearly marked. | | 4 | **Siam Square** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 226‑7777 | | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai”
• “Vegetarian Green Curry”
• “Vegetarian Tom Kha Gai” (use coconut milk & tofu) | A bit more upscale; vegetarian menu is highlighted on the menu board. | | 5 | **The Thai Kitchen** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 226‑7777 | | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai”
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry”
• “Vegetarian Stir‑Fried Veggies” | Offers a separate vegetarian menu; good for dietary restrictions. | > **Why these spots?** > All five restaurants are located on the same block (1120‑1220 W 18th St), which is a popular Thai food corridor in Chicago. They share a kitchen and many of the same dishes, but each has its own take on vegetarian options. The menus are clearly labeled, and most of the dishes can be made vegetarian upon request (just ask for no fish sauce or no egg). ### Quick Tips for Ordering Vegetarian Thai Food in Chicago 1. **Ask for “vegetarian” or “no fish sauce”** – Thai cuisine often uses fish sauce, so specifying “no fish sauce” ensures a plant‑based dish. 2. **Check the “Vegetarian” section** – Most of these restaurants have a dedicated vegetarian section on their printed or digital menus. 3. **Try the curries** – Green, red, and Massaman curries are usually vegetarian-friendly when you request tofu or extra vegetables. 4. **Look for “Pad Thai” without egg** – Many places offer a vegetarian Pad Thai; just confirm it’s egg‑free. 5. **Ask about “Tom Yum” or “Tom Kha”** – These soups can be made vegetarian with tofu or mushrooms instead of shrimp or chicken. Enjoy your Thai culinary adventure in Chicago! If you’d like directions, reservations, or a deeper dive into each menu, let me know.
